docs.title: First five minutes
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/datamllab/HarborRL.git
cd HarborRL
uv sync --extra dev
uv run harborrl hello --out-dir ./harborrl-hello

The walkthrough creates a native task, executes one failing and one passing scripted attempt, runs the actual verifier, and exports training-batch.json. Its token evidence is a fixture: it does not perform inference or update model weights.

Continue with the quick start, or inspect the exact CLI surface.

docs.title: Pipeline at a glance
docs.text:
locked Harbor tasks
        │
        ▼
Claude Code harness ──► Harbor runner ──► verifier reward
        │                     │
        ▼                     ▼
policy gateway / SGLang   audited trajectory evidence
                              │
                              ▼
                    complete GRPO groups
                              │
                              ▼
                    Slime native training

--dry-run, offline validation, CPU tests, and live training establish different levels of evidence. The deployment guides label those boundaries instead of treating a parsed configuration as proof that a GPU run will succeed.

docs.title: Configuration CLI
docs.text: The configuration tools run with the core package (Python 3.10+ and PyYAML). They enumerate implemented capabilities, check configuration offline, and create consistent training schema 2 / deployment schema 1 files. Catalog, preview and validation stay offline. Model preparation explicitly runs the selected Python locally or over SSH to fingerprint an existing tokenizer. It does not download models or allocate Sandbox/GPU jobs.

docs.title: First run without a task JSON or GPU
docs.text:
Install the core package and try the bundled CPU walkthrough:

python -m pip install -e .
harborrl hello --out-dir ./hello-first
harborrl web --workspace ./harborrl-web

Hello World executes two scripted attempts at creating a file, runs the actual task verifier, collects rewards 0 and 1, assembles native IR and exports a GRPO batch. It uses fixture token evidence, marked CONTRACT_READY; it does not perform model inference or update GPU weights. All files stay under the new output directory. The generated catalog.json and claude-code-profile.json can be reused when configuring real training. The command also works from an installed wheel outside a source checkout, on Windows or Linux.

docs.title: Browse and validate
docs.text:
harborrl options
harborrl options deployments --json
harborrl options fields --json
harborrl validate site/config.yaml --deployment site/deployment.yaml --json
harborrl validate site/config.yaml --deployment site/deployment.yaml --check-files

Catalog dimensions are models, algorithms, tasks (task providers), harnesses, datasets, deployments, fields, and compat. JSON keeps the catalog_version and schema_versions envelope when selecting a dimension. The catalog reflects registered implementations, not roadmap claims. Dataset status describes support; available describes local task files. A wheel does not include repository examples, and planned datasets are not ready to train.

Validation defaults to schema, semantics, and cross-file consistency. It does not open referenced profiles or tasks until --check-files is supplied. Run file checks on the controller: its source/interpreter, profile, task catalog and Sandbox configuration belong there. Local GPU and runner paths are checked locally; SSH target paths are deferred. The shared root may be created by a later run and is not required to exist during configuration. Credentials are never read.

Checks are passed, failed, or deferred. The report is invalid if a check fails, otherwise valid_with_deferred_checks while live checks remain. Exit codes are 0 for no failed checks, 1 for validation/creation failure, and 2 for CLI usage errors. --json writes one JSON object to stdout. Schema validators may report only their first error. Without --deployment, the existing CLI discovery of ./deployment.yaml and embedded fallback is preserved and reported.

GPU memory fit, model loading, live tokenizer fingerprints, package versions, connectivity and platform capacity are not established by offline validation. Sandbox image bindings are checked locally; trusted site adapters and credentials are checked later by runner preflight. Sandbox installation/profile timing compatibility is additionally checked by the existing training dry-run.

docs.title: Prepare inputs
docs.text:
1. Obtain Harbor-format tasks and run harborrl hub inspect --tasks-dir /path/tasks --dataset my-tasks --revision pinned-revision --run-dir /path/inspection. The resulting JSONL is an inspection report, not a training catalog. Build a JSON list (or JSONL records with a .jsonl suffix) containing exactly id, revision, path, task_digest, and reward_profile for each selected task. Copy path and task_digest from a NEEDS_PROBE inspection record, assign a unique stable id, retain the pinned revision, and explicitly set the verifier's reward contract (for example reward_profile: {key: reward}). See the catalog example. INVALID and UNSUPPORTED inspection results cannot be made trainable by changing labels. Do not replace computed digests with placeholder values.
  2. Prepare a pinned Claude Code profile. See the native examples for profile structure. It must match the agent and task requirements of your deployment.
  3. Stage checkpoint and reference directories on the GPU target. The wizard calculates both tokenizer fingerprints automatically, using that target's Python with Transformers installed. No manual SHA-256 entry is needed. In Web, choose Prepare model after setting the checkpoint and environment. The operation loads tokenizer files offline with trust_remote_code=False and calls the same fingerprint function as the rollout runtime. A missing dependency or checkpoint produces an actionable error; the draft can still be saved.
  4. Identify controller/GPU/runner Python executables, checkout paths, SSH aliases and shared storage. Service origins must include their declared ports and be reachable by the participating machines.
  5. For Sandbox, prepare the existing platform configuration and image bindings. H-cluster users follow the optional H practice and reference its site file. The core CLI never asks for H project/environment identifiers or embeds private endpoints or credentials.

docs.title: Generate
docs.text:
harborrl init --out-dir ./site-new
harborrl init --answers my-answers.yaml --out-dir ./site-new

Interactive mode explains each required field. Local asks for one shared source directory and Python interpreter, detected from the host running the wizard; Controller, GPU and rollout all use those values. Storage is configured separately. Service modes ask for each remote role and its reachable origins. The wizard prepares model fingerprints automatically, previews both configurations and requires yes to publish.

Progress is saved after every answer to OUT_DIR.draft.json. Type ? for help, :skip to leave a field empty, or :save to save and exit. Ctrl+C or EOF after choosing a deployment also keeps the draft. Resume it later:

harborrl init --out-dir ./site-new --resume ./site-new.draft.json
harborrl init --out-dir ./empty-site --save-draft
harborrl init --out-dir ./local-example --example local
harborrl init --out-dir ./sandbox-example --example sandbox

--example saves a filled reference draft using the current host's detected environment. Replace example paths and hosts before resuming. --draft-file chooses a different progress file. Incomplete drafts never become runnable bundles. Draft updates check revisions and reject stale writers.

Non-terminal generation accepts --answers or --resume. Missing fingerprints trigger explicit tokenizer preparation; --prepare-model recalculates existing values. Missing required answers never fall back to prompting. Use --save-draft to store incomplete answers without running preparation or final validation.

Start from one of these reference answer templates and replace example paths before running:

  • embedded-local: one machine, local Harbor runner, colocated training/serving by default.
  • service-ssh: controller, SSH GPU target and explicit SSH Docker workers.
  • service-sandbox-local-runner: controller and runner here, SSH GPU target, Sandbox task execution.

Templates leave fingerprints empty for automatic preparation. Web also offers filled Local and Sandbox recipes with notes, download and apply actions. GPU allocations illustrate topology; confirm memory requirements for your model before training. For Local Docker, the gateway advertised origin must be reachable inside task containers. On Linux, configure the host-gateway mapping if using host.docker.internal, or choose a reachable host address.

Answers allow only answers_version: 1, preset, training, deployment, and optional sandbox_config and local_environment. Local's local_environment contains source_dir and python and applies to all three roles, taking precedence over advanced per-role overrides. Overrides use the existing schema field names; unknown keys fail. Answer values are not evaluated as shell expressions. Gateway fields, shared run root, GPU budget and worker destinations are derived when only one side is provided. Contradictory explicit values fail. Supply matching origin URLs when changing ports. Paths in training overrides are relative to the final output directory, not the answers file. Deployment machine paths are absolute.

The Sandbox preset can also describe remote runners through an answers file: set training.harbor.runner_transport: ssh and provide deployment rollout workers with docker: false. The builder derives training worker destinations and the first worker's runner Python. All configured interpreters still require preflight.

--probe-local explicitly enables bounded local nvidia-smi UUID and current Python version queries. It also reads explicit SSH Host aliases (no wildcard, Match execution or Include expansion) and gives a parent-directory access hint. Missing tools and failed commands return unknown, not zero GPUs. Suggestions never silently change answers; no remote probe or write permission test occurs.

The output directory must not exist, and its parent must exist. Publication uses an exclusive per-target lock, same-parent staging and a directory rename. Existing files are never overwritten. Failures clean up only this invocation's staging and lock. After an abrupt process termination, inspect any remaining .NAME.init.lock and staging directory before removing them; automatic stale-lock recovery is not attempted. The lock coordinates wizard processes, not arbitrary external writers.

The bundle contains config.yaml, deployment.yaml, and setup-manifest.json. The manifest records schema versions, configuration digests, references and the offline validation scope, including deferred checks. It does not copy credentials.

The CLI prints these next commands without executing them:

harborrl validate site-new/config.yaml --deployment site-new/deployment.yaml --check-files
harborrl train site-new/config.yaml --deployment site-new/deployment.yaml --dry-run
harborrl doctor site-new/config.yaml --deployment site-new/deployment.yaml

doctor performs live environment/connectivity checks. Actual training remains a separate action. Command examples use POSIX shell quoting.

docs.title: Deployment configuration and the controller placement
docs.text:
A deployment.yaml describes where the manager, GPU training target and rollout workers live and how they reach each other; the training YAML keeps every training-side field (learning rate, sampling, task catalog) and is unchanged.

harborrl train train.yaml --deployment deployment.yaml

Without --deployment, a deployment.yaml in the working directory is picked up; when no file exists the compatible embedded-local topology is used and the legacy same-machine behavior is preserved bit-for-bit (recorded in the plan as deployment.source: embedded-local).

docs.title: What the schema covers (v1)
docs.text:
• manager — the HarborRL controller node: embedded or service mode, bind address, control/gateway ports and the URLs other machines use to reach them. In service mode both URLs must be plain origins that match their ports and must not be loopback.
  • gpu_target — the Slime training machine: local or ssh transport, the checkout (source_dir), training interpreter (train_python), an optional controlled environment_file (a JSON variable map, never a shell), and expected_gpus.
  • storage — shared_fs mode with the shared run_root and writability expectations per role.
  • rollout — ssh_docker workers: SSH destination, runner interpreter, Docker requirement and task roots. The embedded provider keeps worker discovery in the training config.
  • connectivity — timeouts and which control-loop hops are required.

Secrets are rejected by the schema: no passwords, keys or API tokens. SSH destinations resolve through the invoking user's SSH config, agent or a restricted identity file. Paths are interpreted in target-machine semantics — the manager never assumes its own sys.executable works on the GPU or workers. See examples/native/deployment-embedded.yaml and examples/native/deployment-service.yaml.

docs.title: Preflight graph
docs.text:
train and doctor share one check graph, executed at the earliest launch stage. Each check records the role and machine it ran against, the outcome, timing, and a user-executable fix. Any failed check exits nonzero before a run directory or training process is created.

Layer order: manager local state (run root, token file, ports) → GPU target (SSH reachability, paths, model paths, visible GPU budget) → rollout workers (SSH, runner Python >= 3.12, pinned Harbor version, Docker, task roots) → control-loop addresses (DNS resolution now, live health dials after components start). --dry-run parses both configs and prints the resolved plan without any remote probing or side effects.

When the GPU target is remote, machine-local dependency probes (Ray, Torch, Slime imports, SGLang image, nvidia-smi) do not run on the manager: they are enforced fail-closed by slime_train.sh at GPU job startup. The manager CPU needs no GPU dependencies.

docs.title: TrainingTarget
docs.text: harborrl/deployment/training_target.py launches one Slime job either as a local child (legacy path) or over SSH (service mode). The SSH target writes a generated gpu-launcher.sh into the shared run directory, starts it detached (setsid) on the GPU machine, records the launcher pid, polls the shared exit-code record, and cancels by signalling the remote process group (INT → TERM → KILL). It never resubmits or restarts a job.

docs.title: RolloutService (manager mode)
docs.text:
harborrl/rollout/service.py is the manager-side control plane: HTTP JSON with run-scoped tokens.

  • GET /healthz, GET /readyz
  • POST /runs/{run_id}/register — idempotent by manifest digest; the same id with a different manifest is a 409.
  • POST /runs/{run_id}/groups — idempotent group submission. Same group id and content returns the existing state; same id with different content is a 409; submitting against a non-admitted policy version is a 409. On timeout the response says running and points at the status endpoint — the client must query, never resubmit.
  • GET /runs/{run_id}/groups/{group_id}, POST .../cancel
  • POST /runs/{run_id}/policy/activate — validates the whole serving pool is healthy on the expected version, drains old admission, then opens the new version and publishes policy-pool.json into the shared run directory.
  • POST /runs/{run_id}/serving/announce — the GPU job publishes its inference endpoint; the manager never hand-configures it.
  • POST /runs/{run_id}/drain, POST /runs/{run_id}/cancel

Bulky data (trajectory manifests, token ids, logprobs, loss masks, group export) is written to the shared run directory. HTTP responses carry paths plus SHA-256 digests; GroupResult also carries per-slot identity, finish reason, reward, trace seal status and verifier digest.

The GPU-side adapter (harborrl/backends/slime_v032/rollout_service_client.py) recomputes every manifest digest, checks identities against the request, requires a complete group of at least two slots on the locked policy version, and only then converts trajectories into Slime samples. It is selected by HARBORRL_ROLLOUT_SERVICE_URL in the GPU job environment.

docs.title: Operational limits
docs.text:
Service mode requires shared storage visible at the configured paths on the controller, GPU target and runners. A successful dry run checks configuration; it does not establish network reachability, available capacity or training quality. Check connectivity with doctor and inspect run artifacts after launch.

Choose worker and group concurrency for the target deployment. Instance readiness does not imply that an agent is running, and a completed checkpoint does not establish learning improvement.

docs.title: GPU Layout
docs.text: deployment.layout: colocate requires equal actor, rollout, and total GPU counts. The Slime launcher passes --colocate only for that layout. Split deployments omit it. The final argv is recorded in the run's command evidence, including in dry-run mode.

docs.title: Trace Memory
docs.text:
Closing an attempt revokes its credential. Sealing still requires every pending request to drain. After trace.json is successfully persisted, the registry releases the full turns and errors. Repeated sealing reads the immutable record from disk. Failed writes retain the payload so sealing can be retried.

The registry retains small attempt records to enforce attempt and credential uniqueness and policy barriers. Training samples retain their current trajectory evidence for as long as the training backend needs those samples.

docs.title: Cleanup Recovery
docs.text:
Docker and Sandbox both stop automatic retries when an attempt produces cleanup-required.json. Queued attempts are checked before starting a Runner; already running attempts finish or are cancelled with cleanup awaited. A runtime also scans its native-rollouts directory before opening the gateway, so restarting the same run cannot bypass unresolved cleanup.

  1. Read each marker reported by the error, including any nested runner/cleanup-required.json. Coordinator markers include the attempt identity and Runner host (null means local execution).
  2. Inspect the matching Harbor Docker or Sandbox resources on that host and confirm that deletion has completed. Retain the attempt's other evidence.
  3. Remove only the markers whose resources have been confirmed clean. Both the attempt-level and nested Runner markers must be resolved.
  4. Restart or resume the run. Admission reopens when no unresolved marker remains.

There is no automatic deletion of potentially live resources during recovery.

docs.title: Embedded Event Loop
docs.text:
Successive synchronous Slime rollout calls reuse one event loop and one cached runtime. The runtime's semaphore and Sandbox admission semaphores belong to that loop. Changing the runtime configuration requires closing the previous runtime. Using a cached runtime from another loop raises RuntimeLifecycleError immediately.

harborrl.rollout.runtime.close_runtime() cancels and awaits outstanding embedded tasks, closes the gateway, then closes async generators, the executor, and the loop. Call it between rollout calls, outside an active event loop; process exit also registers cleanup. The implementation supports Python 3.10. The manager-side RolloutService continues to use its own persistent loop.

docs.title: CPU Regression Checks
docs.text:
These checks use synthetic serving, mock resource allocation, real local Runner subprocesses, shell dry-runs, and stub bootstrap commands. They do not need CUDA, model weights, Docker, Harbor, Slime, or the Sandbox SDK.

python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/harborrl/test_backend_bootstrap.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_native_training.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_native_gateway.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_native_lifecycle.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_native_terminal.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_rollout_runtime.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_rollout_runtime_lifecycle.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_sandbox.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_sandbox_runtime.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_slime_v032_exporter.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_rollout_service.py \
  tests/harborrl/test_delivery_barrier.py

GPU acceptance remains separate: run multi-round split and colocate training, check serving/training memory behavior, verify policy version transitions, and exercise cleanup against actual Docker/Sandbox resources. CPU tests establish the scheduling and lifecycle contracts, not live model or GPU correctness.

docs.title: Sandbox rollout
docs.text: Sandbox is an optional execution environment under the common Controller, RolloutService, Runtime and Harbor Runner. Docker execution remains the default. The core does not import the SDK until an explicitly selected runner needs it.

docs.title: Standard OpenSandbox
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12 or newer for the runner and install pip install -e '.[sandbox]'. Start with examples/native/sandbox.yaml. Set the service origin (without a trailing /v1), a private credential-file reference and exact task image bindings. Standard credentials are opaque tokens, not a platform-specific AK:SK format.

Select the environment in your training config:

harbor:
  python: /opt/harborrl/runner/bin/python
  version: 0.23.0
  runner_transport: local
  workers: []
  environment:
    runtime: sandbox
    config: /srv/harborrl/site/sandbox.yaml

For service placement, use rollout.provider: sandbox in the deployment file. A local runner requires an empty deployment worker list. SSH runners require explicit workers, the same shared task/evidence paths and the adapter installed on each runner. Runner placement is independent of the environment provider. The target and route must be validated before claiming that an SSH/Sandbox deployment works on a real platform.

The standard adapter uses Harbor's OpenSandbox implementation and adds durable allocation tracking, bounded lifecycle operations and cleanup-debt records. Custom trusted adapters subclass ManagedOpenSandboxEnvironment and are selected through adapter: module:Class; arbitrary task input cannot select code. Provider settings belong in options and per-image binding options. They must not contain inline secrets. Core plan construction does not import the adapter, read credentials, connect to a platform or allocate instances.

The optional installation block supports a pinned offline Claude binary: mode: offline_binary, version, binary, and its 64-character sha256. Without it, Harbor performs normal agent setup, which can need network access.

docs.title: Concurrency and evidence
docs.text:
max_live_instances bounds all active instances; each image binding has its own limit. Binding capacity is acquired before global capacity to avoid starvation. startup_concurrency separately bounds simultaneous SDK startup using process-shared locks. Shared-filesystem flock support is required when runners use the same lock directory across hosts.

Groups use the same identity, policy barrier, verifier and consumption audit as Docker. Failed slots cancel their group siblings; submitted independent groups finish before a partial batch is rejected. Unconfirmed cleanup blocks new admission. Production export never accepts synthetic evidence.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
python scripts/sandbox_sdk_contract.py checks installed APIs and fake lifecycle cleanup without contacting a platform. sandbox_probe checks the selected adapter, SDK, credential-file permissions and optional binary locally. Its explicit --network mode is adapter-specific and reports skipped checks.

python scripts/sandbox_smoke.py CONFIG --output NEW_DIRECTORY --gateway URL is a live allocation test and consumes platform resources. A successful CPU test or dependency probe does not establish live training acceptance.

For Brainbox and developer-mediated networking, see the independently installable H-cluster practice. H-specific configuration from the experimental branch must be migrated as described there.

docs.title: Train / inference consistency
docs.text:
Consistency checks compare log probabilities of the same response tokens at the same prefix, before an optimizer update. This measures backend drift; it does not measure model quality or full-distribution KL divergence.

The three policies are the observed behavior q, frozen pre-update trainer p0, and current trainer pθ. Backend drift is log p0 - log q; optimization drift is log pθ - log p0. The Native loss remains unchanged. No TIS, clipping correction, or new training objective is introduced.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Native schema 2 accepts an optional consistency mapping. Its default mode is off. Existing configurations remain valid. audit records numerical violations; enforce rejects violations before training or serving admission. Invalid evidence always rejects, including in audit mode. Enforce requires an explicit max_abs_delta. Calibrate tolerances for the actual model, precision, parallel layout and kernels.

consistency:
  mode: audit
  max_abs_delta: null
  max_mean_abs_delta: null
  bad_token_delta: null
  max_bad_fraction: 0.0
  worst_tokens: 8

Native overrides use the existing --set consistency.mode=audit interface. For enforce, configure a deployment-specific max_abs_delta in YAML before loading the configuration. The configuration is preserved in launch evidence.

docs.title: Native Megatron / SGLang
docs.text:
The enabled launcher runs harborrl.consistency.train, which uses the pinned Slime training loop and its supported actor factory. It never edits upstream Slime. The existing pre-update forward supplies actual packed-batch p0 values. Immutable serving sidecars bind token IDs, float32-normalized behavior scores, response masks, policy version, tokenizer and template identity. Missing or mismatched sidecars reject the batch.

Before each weight synchronization, the actor evaluates two fixed token fixtures using Megatron. Every synchronized SGLang engine then teacher-forces those exact sequences. Generation-time and post-probe versions must both match. Each engine must satisfy the numerical limits independently. Checks also cover the final sync, even when no subsequent rollout occurs. Probe records are reused only for the same pool, configuration and immutable reference. A fixed canary is a smoke check; actual rollout-batch checks provide broader coverage.

Supported initial scope: dense models, synchronous full NCCL synchronization, PP=CP=1, with TP and DP. Temperature and top-p must be 1; top-k must be disabled. Critic, old-actor queues, MoE, release-train and routing replay are rejected. Transformed sampling would require a separate definition of behavior scores.

RUN_DIR/consistency contains sync references, pool admissions, serving-turn sidecars and batch-*.json reports. References include a bounded sampled parameter fingerprint per rank; this is not a full weight checksum. Reports contain valid-token-weighted absolute/signed errors, log-ratio range, bad-token fraction, bounded worst positions and histogram percentile upper bounds. They do not copy raw prompt or response text. TP duplicate counts are excluded. Distributed validation collects rank errors before all ranks reject.

docs.title: Validation and limitations
docs.text:
Run pytest -q tests/test_consistency.py for the dependency-free checks. With Torch installed, run pytest -q tests/test_consistency_torch.py for two-rank failure propagation. These tests do not run a separate training loop.

GPU acceptance must additionally exercise the locked Megatron / SGLang versions on the target hardware: initial sync, actual rollout tokens, optimizer update, final sync and checkpoint resume. Record dtype, attention backend, TP/DP, model revision and measured error distribution. CPU tests and mocked HTTP responses cannot certify SGLang input-logprob behavior or CUDA numerical tolerances. This implementation has not yet passed that live GPU acceptance gate.

H-cluster relay topology remains a deployment practice. No H-cluster hostnames, private paths or machine-specific numerical thresholds belong in this module.

docs.title: Local web console
docs.text:
harborrl web --workspace ./harborrl-web

This opens a browser on an available loopback port. Keep the terminal running. --port 8765 chooses a fixed port; --no-browser prints the URL without opening it. The workspace stores drafts, saved configuration bundles and execution records. One console process owns a workspace at a time. The web console uses the core Python dependencies; Node, a frontend build and CDN access are not required.

docs.title: Configure and launch
docs.text:
1. New users can first select Run Hello World. It needs no task JSON, model or GPU and opens the Runs view with actual execution logs. This CPU walkthrough runs scripted attempts and a real verifier, then exports a GRPO batch using clearly marked fixture tokens; it does not run model inference or training.
  2. Open Local example or Sandbox example to view, download or apply a filled best-practice recipe. Replace example model paths and service hostnames. In Local, source directory and Python are detected on the machine running the console and edited once for Controller, GPU and rollout. Storage is separate. SSH workers and Sandbox expose the paths belonging to their remote roles.
  3. Provide checkpoint/reference directories. Use bundled Hello World task & profile creates valid input files locally, or supply your own pinned catalog and profile. Select Prepare model to calculate both fingerprints using the real tokenizer and selected GPU Python, over SSH when needed. No manual SHA-256 entry is shown. Changing the checkpoint or target environment clears the old fingerprints. See the CLI guide for prerequisites.
  4. Choose GPU layout, tensor parallelism, rollout batches and sampling settings. Allocation defaults are configuration values, not a model memory-fit estimate.
  5. Review the generated YAML and validation. Missing fields appear in a prominent list with bold labels, help and links that focus the relevant input. Required inputs also have inline explanations. Check local files additionally checks references on the controller. Deferred GPU, connectivity, model and Sandbox checks remain explicit. Create runnable configuration publishes the validated bundle.
  6. Run Dry-run to build the actual CLI launch plan. Doctor performs live checks after confirmation. Start training requires a separate confirmation and invokes the existing harborrl train flow, including its preflight.

Configuration names are limited to letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. Use Save draft at any step, including an empty or incomplete configuration. Drafts appear separately from Runnable configurations in the sidebar; reopen one to continue and save another revision under the same name. They survive server restarts. Stale revisions from another tab are rejected so work is not silently overwritten. Drafts cannot start Dry-run, Doctor or training.

Runnable configurations are immutable. Reopen one to launch it again, or edit it and publish a new numbered version. The advanced answers editor and YAML/JSON import use the existing answers_version: 1 contract. Download an individual generated file or export answers from the editor. Advanced remote Sandbox runners can be specified through imported answers; the form preset defaults to a local runner.

H-cluster deployments remain the optional H practice. Prepare its Sandbox configuration separately and reference the path. H project/environment identifiers and relay settings are not part of the core web form.

Windows supports configuration and dry-run. Live training/doctor controls require the console to run on a POSIX controller, using the same environment and checkout that would normally run the training CLI. Deployment readiness still depends on the project's supported Linux training environment.

docs.title: Runs and shutdown
docs.text:
Only one execution is active per workspace, including Hello World, doctor and dry-run. This prevents duplicate launches within this console; it is not a cluster-wide GPU scheduler. Other CLI processes or different workspaces can still use the same resources, and operators must coordinate those allocations.

Each job keeps immutable input files and a durable job.json/console.log under WORKSPACE/jobs/JOB_ID. Execution appends web/JOB_ID to the configured shared run root and updates both config files in its snapshot. The original saved bundle is unchanged. The existing runtime then creates its normal training/... run directory there. This isolates artifacts while retaining the configured shared filesystem. Run logs show the actual snapshot and output paths.

The Runs view polls status and the last 64 KiB of output. Controller shows the CLI output and errors. GPU training reads the separate train-stdout.log when the service deployment creates one. Embedded training generally streams into the controller log. Full logs remain on disk; the browser download contains the currently displayed tail. This initial release does not aggregate WandB curves or claim remote/GPU progress from a quiet controller log.

Stop sends an interrupt through the existing CLI lifecycle. Local training forwards it to the training process group; service mode uses the existing SSH target cancellation. stopping means cleanup is pending, not that resources are already free. Closing the browser does not stop a job. Ctrl+C or SIGTERM in the server terminal requests cleanup; shutdown waits up to 30 seconds. A timeout records an unknown state without force-killing arbitrary remote processes.

After a crash or interrupted shutdown, previously running jobs appear as unknown. New launches are blocked. Inspect the target processes, shared run records and Sandbox cleanup evidence, then use Confirm cleanup to acknowledge that external cleanup is complete. This action records operator confirmation; it does not kill a stored PID or automatically relaunch a job. The server never signals a PID recovered from an old session.

docs.title: Remote controller
docs.text:
On the controller, from the intended checkout/environment:

python -m harborrl.cli web --workspace /srv/shared/web-console --port 8765 --no-browser

On the workstation, create a local SSH forward:

ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:8765:127.0.0.1:8765 your-controller-alias

Open the URL printed by the controller in the workstation browser. If the local forward uses a different port, replace only the URL port. Leave the #token=... fragment intact. If either port is occupied, choose an unused port; omitting --port selects one automatically and prints it.

The listener is deliberately fixed to 127.0.0.1. A random per-session token protects API reads and writes; the browser moves the URL fragment into sessionStorage and removes it from the address bar. State-changing requests also require a same-origin JSON request. Responses use CSP, frame blocking and no-store headers, and assets are packaged locally. Keep the token private: this is a local single-user console with the controller user's filesystem and training privileges. It is not a public multi-user service or an Internet-facing gateway. Do not expose it through a public reverse proxy.

docs.title: AI agent deployment and training verification protocol
docs.text: This document is the authoritative protocol for an AI agent that helps a user deploy HarborRL and verify whether the user's machines can run training. Follow it before searching for unrelated instructions or improvising installation steps.

docs.title: Practiced deployment workflow
docs.text:
Use this workflow as the default unless the user supplies a stricter site process. It deliberately separates diagnosis, approved repair, and acceptance.

  1. Ask for or infer the target topology and config path. Run only read-only checks until the user approves a change.
  2. Return the structured report from this protocol, including every confirmed blocker and every unknown check. Do not replace the report with a prose-only summary.
  3. Propose the smallest next command that removes one blocker. Stop and wait for explicit user consent before installing, downloading, pulling, mounting, or starting anything.
  4. After each approved change, rerun the affected phase and the repository doctor. Never assume that a command succeeded.
  5. For native training, finish with a doctor run and launcher dry run. Report static deployment as accepted only when both pass and every statically verifiable machine check is ready. An unstarted live gateway remains an explicit deferred item rather than a silent pass.
  6. Start real training only after the user confirms resource consumption and the intended scope. A successful dry run is not permission to launch training.

docs.title: Acceptance levels
docs.text:
Use one of these levels in the final report so the user can tell whether the agent verified the target they actually chose:

Level Meaning Required evidence cpu_development The controller can develop and test HarborRL Phase 1 passes, harborrl --help works, repository tests pass deployment_preflight The configured cross-machine deployment is statically ready Every statically verifiable role and machine check passes, doctor reports no failed checks, and the CLI dry run resolves the plan training A real training launch passed the user-selected smoke scope Training artifacts or logs show the selected scope completed; list any explicitly deferred live checks separately

Do not label a CPU-only result as deployment_preflight. Do not label a dry run as training. Live-service checks may remain unknown only when they are not part of the selected acceptance level; they must still appear in not_checked. If evidence for the selected level is incomplete, its acceptance verdict is unknown even when individual installation checks pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Determine the readiness of each required machine role, report confirmed missing dependencies and resources, and propose the smallest safe next action. Do not equate “the repository cloned successfully” or “unit tests pass” with “native GPU training is ready.”

Evaluate these roles separately:

Role Purpose GPU requirement CPU development machine Clone HarborRL, create the locked environment, run CLI and tests No Harbor rollout worker Execute isolated Harbor tasks and verifiers in Docker No NVIDIA GPU required Native GPU training machine Run Slime/Megatron/SGLang training and policy serving Yes Controller Read the YAML config and launch HarborRL No GPU requirement of its own, but it must reach every selected service

A deployment may combine these roles on one machine or split them across machines. In particular, Harbor task rollout workers can be CPU machines while policy serving and training run on a GPU machine.

docs.title: Safety and evidence rules
docs.text:
1. Identify the target topology before changing the environment.
  2. Start with read-only inspection commands. Do not install packages, pull images, download model weights, start services, or write configuration without the user's explicit consent.
  3. Never expose or request provider API keys, SSH private keys, passwords, or tokens. Command output and paths are sufficient for this protocol.
  4. Use three verdict values:
  5. ready: every required check passed.
  6. not_ready: at least one requirement is confirmed missing.
  7. unknown: the agent lacks access, the user has not supplied a path or topology, or a check is intentionally deferred until a live service runs.
  8. Never turn an unchecked item into a pass. unknown is a valid conclusion.
  9. Record the exact command, exit status, and concise evidence for failures.
  10. After environment changes, rerun the relevant checks rather than assuming the change succeeded.

docs.title: Required input
docs.text:
If the user does not already provide this information, ask only for the missing items that block diagnosis:

  • Whether the target is CPU development only, deployment/doctor validation, or an actual training run.
  • Whether rollout workers and GPU training are on one machine or different machines.
  • The training YAML path and deployment YAML path, when they exist.
  • SSH host aliases and the absolute HarborRL checkout path on each rollout worker.
  • The absolute paths of the model actor/reference checkpoints and the output filesystem when GPU training is in scope.

Do not ask for credentials. Existing local SSH configuration must be used.

docs.title: Phase 1: CPU development baseline
docs.text:
Run these read-only checks from the HarborRL checkout:

git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
uv --version
uv lock --check
uv sync --extra dev --dry-run

Interpretation:

  • uv must be version 0.9 or newer.
  • uv lock --check must report that uv.lock is up to date.
  • The dry run must be able to resolve Python 3.10 or newer and the locked development dependencies.
  • Uncommitted changes are not an environment failure, but report them because they can make reproduction ambiguous.

With user consent, create or update the locked environment and verify the CLI:

uv sync --extra dev
uv run harborrl --help

Only after that setup should the agent run repository tests. A CPU-only machine that passes these checks is cpu_development=ready; it is not necessarily ready for native GPU training.

docs.title: Phase 2: Interpret the deployment topology
docs.text:
When a YAML config exists, read these fields before running commands:

  • harbor.python: absolute Python interpreter used by every rollout worker.
  • harbor.version: required Harbor version; the current native contract uses 0.23.0.
  • harbor.workers: SSH host aliases used by the controller.
  • gateway.advertised_url: URL that rollout workers must reach.
  • gateway.host and gateway.port: listener binding.
  • model.checkpoint and model.reference: paths consumed by the GPU runtime.
  • deployment.num_gpus, actor_gpus, rollout_gpus, actor_tensor_parallel_size, rollout_gpus_per_engine, and layout.
  • tasks.catalog, harness.profile, and output.root.

For every absolute path, verify it on the machine that consumes it. Do not assume that two machines share a filesystem merely because they can SSH to one another. If a shared filesystem is claimed, verify that the path and expected content are visible from both sides.

The remote runner is launched with a command equivalent to:

ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ClearAllForwardings=yes \
  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new WORKER \
  'cd /absolute/Harbor-RL && exec /absolute/harbor/python -m harborrl.rollout.harbor_job.runner'

Therefore each rollout worker needs the HarborRL source tree at the same absolute path used by the controller, unless the user provides a corrected site-specific launch arrangement.

docs.title: Phase 3: CPU Harbor rollout worker checks
docs.text:
From the controller, check noninteractive SSH and worker identity first:

ssh -o BatchMode=yes WORKER 'uname -a && pwd'
ssh -o BatchMode=yes WORKER 'test -d /absolute/Harbor-RL && echo repo-present'

Then run the repository-native probe using the YAML worker and interpreter values:

ssh -o BatchMode=yes WORKER \
  'cd /absolute/Harbor-RL && /absolute/harbor/python -m harborrl.rollout.harbor_job.runner --probe'

A passing probe must:

  • exit with status 0,
  • report Python 3.12.0 or newer,
  • report harbor_version: 0.23.0,
  • report usable Harbor ClaudeCodeOptions, TrialConfig, and Trial APIs.

Also check Docker from the worker's normal environment:

docker version
docker info

The Docker daemon must be reachable by the Harbor worker. A worker without an NVIDIA GPU is acceptable; a worker without a usable Docker daemon is not.

Task images may only be discovered while executing a task. If an image has not been pulled, report image availability as unknown, not as failed. Network or registry failures observed during the first live task are rollout-worker failures even though model training itself may be healthy.

Finally, verify DNS/routing for the hostname in gateway.advertised_url. If the gateway is not running yet, report connectivity as unknown. A connection refused or timeout after the gateway is running is a failure.

docs.title: Phase 4: Native GPU training checks
docs.text:
On the GPU machine, run:

nvidia-smi
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv,noheader
printf 'CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=%s\n' "${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-<unset>}"
df -h .

Check all of the following:

  • nvidia-smi exits successfully.
  • The number of visible GPUs is at least deployment.num_gpus.
  • For layout: split, actor_gpus + rollout_gpus <= num_gpus.
  • For layout: colocate, actor_gpus == rollout_gpus == num_gpus.
  • actor_gpus is divisible by actor_tensor_parallel_size.
  • rollout_gpus is divisible by rollout_gpus_per_engine.
  • The model attention-head configuration is compatible with both parallel sizes; harborrl doctor performs this check when the checkpoint is readable.
  • The checkpoint/output filesystem has at least 128 GiB free unless the user explicitly changes the launcher's checkpoint minimum. Report lower free space as not_ready.

GPU count alone does not prove that a specific model fits. Unless model size, checkpoint metadata, sequence length, and available accelerator memory give a defensible estimate, report model memory fit as unknown.

The pinned backend stack is normally installed with:

bash scripts/bootstrap_backends.sh /path/to/harborrl-backends
. /path/to/harborrl-backends/harborrl-backend.env

Treat the bootstrap as a mutating, network-heavy operation and request consent first. After sourcing harborrl-backend.env, verify:

  • SLIME_DIR is a directory containing train.py.
  • MEGATRON_DIR is a directory when set; it may be omitted when the official Slime image supplies Megatron.
  • SGLANG_IMAGE names the pinned image expected by this repository.
  • Docker can inspect the image; if not, mark it missing or not yet pulled.
  • The training Python environment can import the packages and backend hooks checked by harborrl doctor.

docs.title: Phase 5: Cross-machine deployment checks
docs.text:
For a CPU-rollout/GPU-training split, verify each direction independently:

  1. Controller to every Harbor worker: noninteractive SSH and the runner probe.
  2. Every Harbor worker to gateway.advertised_url: hostname resolution and TCP connectivity once the gateway is running.
  3. GPU machine to model/reference checkpoint paths and writable output root.
  4. Controller to paths needed to materialize catalogs and launch artifacts.
  5. Worker to every task path referenced by the catalog.
  6. All machines to any image registry required by their assigned task.

Do not use localhost evidence from one machine to approve a service on another machine. If the agent can inspect only the controller, mark remote checks as unknown and tell the user which command must run on which host.

docs.title: Phase 6: Repository doctor
docs.text:
After the CPU environment exists and a YAML config is available, run from the controller:

uv run harborrl doctor --config path/to/config.yaml \
  --deployment path/to/deployment.yaml

Omit --deployment only when the target intentionally uses the implicit embedded/default topology. The native launcher wrapper has no --deployment option and changes to the repository root, so use it only when that discovery behavior is intended:

bash scripts/launch_native.sh --config path/to/config.yaml --doctor

For deployment_preflight acceptance, also run the safe launcher dry run and retain its resolved plan as evidence:

uv run harborrl train path/to/config.yaml \
  --deployment path/to/deployment.yaml --dry-run

Requirements:

  • Parse the JSON object from stdout; do not rely only on the exit code.
  • Treat every check with ok: false as a failure.
  • Preserve the check's path, service, dependency, resource, or task identity in the final report.
  • Remember that doctor explicitly defers the live serving semantic probe. A passing doctor therefore validates configuration and static preflight, not a complete training outcome.

Do not start a training run merely because doctor passes. Ask the user for the intended validation scope and confirm resource consumption first.

docs.title: Required agent report
docs.text:
End the diagnosis with a concise human summary followed by this JSON shape:

{
  "protocol": "harborrl/environment-check",
  "protocol_version": 2,
  "repo_commit": "string or null",
  "verdict": "ready | not_ready | unknown",
  "acceptance": {
    "level": "cpu_development | deployment_preflight | training",
    "verdict": "ready | not_ready | unknown",
    "evidence": [
      "uv run harborrl --help exited 0",
      "uv run pytest exited 0"
    ]
  },
  "roles": {
    "cpu_development": "ready | not_ready | unknown",
    "harbor_rollout_worker": "ready | not_ready | unknown",
    "gpu_training": "ready | not_ready | unknown",
    "cross_machine_deployment": "ready | not_ready | unknown"
  },
  "machines": [
    {
      "name": "user-provided alias",
      "roles": ["controller", "harbor_rollout_worker", "gpu_training"],
      "verdict": "ready | not_ready | unknown"
    }
  ],
  "missing": [
    {
      "role": "gpu_training",
      "machine": "gpu-host",
      "item": "visible GPU budget",
      "severity": "required",
      "evidence": "nvidia-smi exited with 127",
      "fix": "Install the NVIDIA driver and rerun nvidia-smi."
    }
  ],
  "not_checked": [
    {
      "item": "live gateway connectivity",
      "reason": "gateway was not running during the initial diagnosis"
    }
  ],
  "doctor": {
    "executed": true,
    "passed": false,
    "failed_checks": []
  }
}

Omit roles that the user explicitly excludes from the target, and explain the omission in the human summary. A top-level verdict is ready only when every role required by the user's stated target is ready. Otherwise use not_ready when at least one required role has a confirmed blocker, or unknown when readiness cannot be established.

The acceptance.verdict is scoped to the selected acceptance level. For example, deployment_preflight can be ready while the top-level verdict is unknown because a live gateway semantic probe is intentionally deferred; that deferred probe must remain visible in not_checked.

docs.title: Embedded and local deployment
docs.text: Embedded mode keeps controller and training lifecycle in one process placement while allowing Harbor runners to be local or SSH workers. It is the compatibility default when no deployment file is supplied.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
For this command:

harborrl train site/config.yaml --dry-run

HarborRL resolves deployment in this order:

  1. an explicit --deployment PATH;
  2. deployment.yaml in the current directory; or
  3. a generated embedded-local deployment derived from the training config.

The generated deployment uses the current checkout and interpreter, the configured output root, training-config worker destinations, and the configured GPU count. Its source is recorded as embedded-local in the plan.

docs.title: Explicit embedded file
docs.text:
Use an explicit schema-1 file when you want the topology recorded independently:

harborrl train site/config.yaml \
  --deployment examples/native/deployment-embedded.yaml \
  --dry-run

The repository example contains absolute container-style placeholders. Replace them before doctor or a live run.

docs.title: Local runner configuration
docs.text:
To run the Harbor runner on the controller:

harbor:
  python: /absolute/path/to/python3.12
  version: "0.23.0"
  runner_transport: local
  workers: []
  environment:
    runtime: docker

The gateway's advertised_url must still be reachable from task containers. On Linux, configure a host-gateway mapping before using host.docker.internal, or use a reachable host address.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Embedded placement does not remove the need for GPUs, model files, backend dependencies, Docker workers, or network routes.
  • An implicit deployment does not activate the full explicit topology preflight layer; use a deliberate deployment file for cross-machine acceptance.
  • Each run uses a new directory. HarborRL does not resume by reusing an arbitrary completed run directory.

docs.title: H-cluster practice
docs.text: The optional practices/h_cluster package adapts HarborRL to Brainbox and restricted Sandbox egress. It reuses the core controller, RolloutService, Harbor runner, trajectory audit, and training path; it is not installed with the core package and does not provide another algorithm.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
GPU training adapter ──► developer Controller / RolloutService
                                  │
                                  ▼
                         local Harbor runner ──► Sandbox platform

Sandbox Claude ──► loopback mailbox ◄── developer relay pump
                                             │
                                             ▼
                                   developer Gateway ──► GPU SGLang

The developer initiates authenticated platform-proxy requests. A Sandbox instance does not need a direct route to the GPU or developer-private listener. Relay responses, including server-sent events, are fully buffered.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12 or newer in the runner environment:

python -m pip install -e . -e practices/h_cluster

Start from practices/h_cluster/configs/deployment.example.yaml and practices/h_cluster/configs/sandbox.example.yaml. Use service placement, a local developer runner, and no SSH rollout workers. In the training file, set:

harbor:
  runner_transport: local
  workers: []
  environment:
    runtime: sandbox
    config: /absolute/path/to/site/sandbox.yaml

Install the practice in the runner environment. The controller may use a separate Python environment for tokenizer and service dependencies.

For every task image, create a matching platform Environment:

  • expose command port 44772 and the configured relay port;
  • set capacity high enough for the binding limit and use prewarm 0 for an idle test deployment;
  • pin the image and offline Claude binary hash;
  • prepare external task/verifier dependencies inside the image; and
  • keep AK:SK credentials in the referenced mode-600 file, never in YAML or Git.

The model relay is not a general internet proxy. The developer must reach the platform proxy and every advertised inference endpoint, and the GPU must reach the controller.

docs.title: Validate locally
docs.text:
python -m pip install -e '.[dev]' -e practices/h_cluster
python -m pytest practices/h_cluster/tests
python scripts/sandbox_sdk_contract.py

These tests use local HTTP/mock contracts. They do not allocate platform instances or prove GPU connectivity.

docs.title: Probe a configured site
docs.text:
After filling private site files, use the runner interpreter:

python -m harborrl.rollout.harbor_job.sandbox_probe \
  /absolute/path/to/site/sandbox.yaml

python -m harborrl.rollout.harbor_job.sandbox_probe \
  /absolute/path/to/site/sandbox.yaml --network

harborrl train /absolute/path/to/site/config.yaml \
  --deployment /absolute/path/to/site/deployment.yaml --dry-run

The first probe is local. --network performs authenticated, read-only Environment checks and creates no instances. The dry run parses the plan without contacting the GPU. Confirm actual routes before removing --dry-run.

Endpoint GET 502, 503, and 504 responses are retried within the creation deadline; the allocation POST is never retried. A platform Pending state can still time out and must not be reported as ready capacity.

docs.title: Migrate an experimental config
docs.text:
Flat experimental Brainbox configuration is intentionally not accepted by the standard OpenSandbox schema:

  1. Replace provider: brainbox with adapter: harborrl_h_cluster.environment:BrainboxEnvironment.
  2. Move project and relay settings under top-level options.
  3. Move Environment IDs and mount requirements under each binding's options.
  4. Keep lifecycle limits and offline installation in their common top-level fields.
  5. Keep the platform command port fixed at 44772.

docs.title: Cleanup and scaling
docs.text:
After cancellation, inspect instance lifecycle evidence and every cleanup-required.json marker. Verify both the live instance list and Environment capacity before reuse; an empty list can disagree with capacity accounting. Never delete templates or instances owned by another run.

Start with one serial complete group. Increase concurrency only after confirming binding limits, project quotas, relay behavior, verifier dependencies, and cleanup. Allocated or Running instances do not prove that an agent is executing, and a checkpoint or policy-version change does not prove learning improvement.

docs.title: Read the full practice guide
docs.text:
The source package remains the authoritative implementation-specific guide and configuration reference:

H-cluster deployment practice

H-cluster hostnames, IDs, credentials, mounts, and numerical thresholds are site-specific and intentionally absent from the core schema.

docs.title: Controller and SSH service deployment
docs.text: Service mode separates the manager/controller, GPU training target, and rollout workers. The controller hosts the RolloutService and policy gateway; rollout providers execute tasks independently. Training dispatch always uses the SSH target; gpu_target.transport: local resolves to localhost SSH rather than a local child.

docs.title: Start from the example
docs.text:
Copy and edit the service deployment example. All paths use target-machine semantics and must be absolute.

harborrl validate site/config.yaml \
  --deployment site/deployment.yaml --check-files

harborrl train site/config.yaml \
  --deployment site/deployment.yaml --dry-run

harborrl doctor site/config.yaml \
  --deployment site/deployment.yaml

docs.title: Required routes
docs.text:
Source Destination Purpose GPU target manager.control_url Register run, submit groups, announce serving Rollout workers manager.gateway_url Harness model requests Manager announced GPU inference endpoint Policy serving control/data path Manager GPU target over SSH (including localhost for local) Launch, poll, and cancel training Manager rollout workers over SSH Probe and run ssh_docker workers

Service manager origins must be non-loopback plain HTTP(S) origins matching their declared ports.

docs.title: Shared filesystem
docs.text:
Only shared_fs storage is implemented. The configured storage.run_root must be visible and writable as declared by the manager, GPU target, and workers. Bulky trajectory and training data travel through that root; control responses carry paths and SHA-256 digests.

Do not assume that identical path strings imply a shared mount. Verify visibility and writability from every consuming machine.

docs.title: SSH behavior
docs.text:
SSH targets use the invoking user's SSH configuration and agent. Schema fields may reference a restricted identity file, but never contain passwords or private-key contents. Commands disable forwarding and use noninteractive operation.

The service GPU target writes gpu-launcher.sh into the shared run directory, starts it detached, records its PID and exit code, and cancels its process group with escalating signals. HarborRL does not automatically resubmit a failed training job. Only the embedded path uses LocalTrainingTarget as a direct child process.

docs.title: Rollout providers
docs.text:
• ssh_docker requires at least one explicit worker with task roots, source checkout, runner Python, and Docker access.
  • sandbox uses the optional environment provider and may have local or SSH runners.
  • embedded preserves worker discovery from the training configuration.

Start with one complete group and inspect cleanup evidence before increasing concurrency.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: HarborRL separates portable CPU contracts from site-specific GPU and worker requirements. You can learn the data flow and validate a configuration before installing the native backend stack.

docs.title: Choose a path
docs.text: Goal Start here Requires Understand the pipeline CPU Hello World Python 3.10+ Prepare a real configuration Configuration CLI Existing task/profile/model paths Inspect Harbor tasks Task tutorial Local Harbor-format task files Resolve a native launch plan Native dry run Example files only Check a target deployment Environment verification Access to configured machines Start GPU training Native training Pinned backend stack, GPUs, workers

docs.title: The core flow
docs.text:
1. A strict schema-2 training file selects one registered model, algorithm, task provider, and harness.
  2. A strict schema-1 deployment file places the controller, GPU target, shared storage, and rollout workers. If it is omitted, HarborRL derives an embedded-local topology.
  3. The controller validates the configuration and builds a launch plan.
  4. Harbor runners execute locked tasks. The policy gateway records requests, responses, raw log probabilities, policy versions, and consumption evidence.
  5. Verifier rewards and complete groups are exported to the pinned Slime GRPO backend; equal-reward groups produce zero advantages.

docs.title: What each check proves
docs.text:
Check What it establishes What it does not establish harborrl validate Offline schema, semantic, and cross-file consistency Connectivity, GPU capacity, model loading harborrl train ... --dry-run Referenced inputs load and a launch plan resolves Remote readiness or resource availability harborrl doctor Configured environment and topology checks Training quality or a completed run CPU test suite Scheduling, evidence, export, and lifecycle contracts Live CUDA, SGLang, or model numerics Live training evidence The selected smoke scope actually ran Generalized learning improvement

A dry run is intentionally side-effect free

It does not contact remote machines or allocate GPU/Sandbox resources. Run doctor for live checks and obtain operator approval before starting training.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text: The core package supports Python 3.10 or newer. CPU development and the Hello World walkthrough do not require Linux. Native GPU training, Docker-based Harbor workers, and the optional Sandbox runner have additional platform and Python requirements; see installation and deployment.

docs.title: CPU development environment
docs.text:
Install Python 3.10 or newer and uv 0.9 or newer. From the repository root:

uv sync --extra dev
uv run harborrl --help
uv run pytest

uv sync uses the checked-in uv.lock and creates .venv/. The core environment does not install CUDA kernels, Docker, model weights, Harbor, Slime, Megatron-LM, or SGLang.

For an editable pip installation instead:

python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
python -m pytest

docs.title: Optional Sandbox runner
docs.text:
The standard OpenSandbox integration requires Python 3.12 or newer in the runner environment:

python -m pip install -e '.[sandbox]'
python scripts/sandbox_sdk_contract.py

The contract script checks installed APIs and a fake lifecycle; it does not connect to a platform or prove that a live allocation works. Continue with the OpenSandbox guide.

docs.title: Native training backends
docs.text:
Native training uses a pinned external Slime/Megatron/SGLang stack. Install it in a writable location outside the repository:

bash scripts/bootstrap_backends.sh "/absolute/path/to/harborrl-backends"
. "/absolute/path/to/harborrl-backends/harborrl-backend.env"

The generated environment file provides SLIME_DIR, MEGATRON_DIR, and SGLANG_IMAGE to child processes. The bootstrap is network- and storage-intensive; inspect the script and obtain site approval before running it on managed machines.

After preparing a valid training and deployment pair, source the generated environment and resolve the explicit plan:

uv run harborrl train /absolute/path/to/config.yaml \
  --deployment /absolute/path/to/deployment.yaml \
  --dry-run

Remove --dry-run only after harborrl doctor passes and the operator has approved resource consumption. scripts/launch_native.sh is a convenience wrapper for the embedded/default-discovery path; it has no --deployment option and will bootstrap the directory passed with --backends when its environment file is absent.

docs.title: Documentation environment
docs.text:
The documentation toolchain is separate from the Python 3.10 runtime support matrix and is validated with Python 3.12:

python -m pip install -e . -r docs/requirements.txt
python -m mkdocs build --strict
python -m mkdocs serve

The strict build treats broken internal links, missing navigation entries, and other MkDocs warnings as errors.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This path starts with a CPU-only executable lesson, inspects the registered support surface, and finishes with a side-effect-free native launch plan.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: uv sync --extra dev

docs.title: 2. Run Hello World
docs.text:
Choose a directory that does not already exist:

uv run harborrl hello --out-dir ./harborrl-hello

Expected final output includes PASS, rewards [0, 1], and the location of the artifacts. This executes a real local verifier and exports a GRPO batch with fixture tokens. It does not call a model or update weights.

Inspect the summary and batch:

uv run python -m json.tool harborrl-hello/hello-result.json
uv run python -m json.tool harborrl-hello/training-batch.json

docs.title: 3. Query the registry
docs.text:
uv run harborrl list models
uv run harborrl list algorithms
uv run harborrl list tasks
uv run harborrl list harnesses

list always emits JSON. For field descriptions, datasets, deployment presets, and compatibility constraints, use the richer offline catalog:

uv run harborrl options
uv run harborrl options fields --json

docs.title: 4. Validate the bundled configuration
docs.text:
uv run harborrl validate examples/native/train_qwen_native.yaml \
  --deployment examples/native/deployment-embedded.yaml \
  --json

The example is structurally valid but contains placeholder model and environment paths. A valid_with_deferred_checks result is expected: offline validation does not claim that the target GPU, services, or checkpoints are ready.

docs.title: 5. Resolve a launch plan
docs.text:
uv run harborrl train examples/native/train_qwen_native.yaml \
  --deployment examples/native/deployment-embedded.yaml \
  --dry-run

The command loads the harness profile and task catalog, applies schema validation, selects the registered MATH components, and prints the resolved plan. It performs no remote probes and starts no training process.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Build a site-specific bundle with the configuration CLI.
  • Learn the exact MATH compatibility rules.
  • Follow the native training workflow.
  • Choose an embedded or service topology.

docs.title: MATH components
docs.text: MATH means Models × Algorithms × Tasks × Harnesses. HarborRL represents each dimension with an explicit registry entry and rejects incompatible combinations before launch.

docs.title: Current registry
docs.text:
Dimension ID Implementation Key constraint Model qwen Qwen adapter, SGLang serving model.args_file starts with qwen Algorithm grpo Slime GRPO Complete groups of at least two samples Task provider native_harbor JSON catalog Native Harbor task locks Task provider harbor_jsonl JSONL catalog One complete task lock on every line; no blanks Harness claude_code Claude Code Harbor 0.23.0, exact CLI version

Query the installed package rather than relying on a static list:

harborrl list models
harborrl list algorithms
harborrl list tasks
harborrl list harnesses
harborrl options compat --json

docs.title: Compatibility checks
docs.text:
For a selected configuration, HarborRL verifies that:

  • the model and algorithm both support the backend contract;
  • the task provider supports execution.backend;
  • the selected Harbor version is supported by the harness;
  • model and harness tool protocols match;
  • the model gateway exposes the harness request protocol;
  • the sample group meets the algorithm's minimum size; and
  • audited raw log probabilities are enabled when the algorithm requires them.

These checks establish interface compatibility, not model quality, memory fit, or a successful live run.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Tokenizer/template identity, SGLang serving, and Qwen tool-call parsing.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text: GRPO group requirements, advantage computation, and pinned backend hooks.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: Native Harbor format, immutable task locks, and verifier reward profiles.

docs.title: Harnesses
docs.text: Claude Code profile validation, credentials, controls, and session audit.

docs.title: GRPO
docs.text:
grpo is the only registered training algorithm. It uses the slime-v0.3.2-native-v1 backend contract and HarborRL's native advantage, conversion, loss, and post-processing hooks.

training:
  backend_contract: slime-v0.3.2-native-v1
  learning_rate: 0.000001
  num_rollout: 1
  save_interval: 1

sampling:
  group_size: 2
  groups_per_batch: 1
  max_attempts: 2
  max_context: 8192
  max_tokens: 1024

docs.title: Group contract
docs.text:
Every admitted group must:

  • contain at least two completed trajectories;
  • use the same locked policy version and immutable task identity;
  • carry finite verifier rewards (equal-reward groups are valid and produce zero advantages);
  • carry audited raw model log probabilities and valid loss masks; and
  • pass trajectory, reward-receipt, and consumption-evidence validation.

Advantages are normalized within each complete group. The training reduction is global-sum, and export validates the total token weight before a batch reaches the backend.

sampling.max_attempts bounds retries for invalid attempts; it is not a retry budget for low rewards.

docs.title: Backend hooks
docs.text:
HarborRL maps the contract to pinned Slime hook implementations for:

  • rollout generation;
  • sample-to-training-data conversion;
  • advantage and return computation;
  • clipped policy-gradient loss; and
  • rollout-data post-processing.

The launcher validates the hook assignment and backend versions. It does not edit the upstream Slime checkout.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• DAPO and other algorithms are not registered.
  • Only the Slime v0.3.2 native hook contract is accepted.
  • CPU tests validate numerical and structural contracts, not live distributed GPU behavior.

docs.title: Compatibility and evidence
docs.text: HarborRL uses three different sources of compatibility information. They answer different questions.

docs.title: Component registry
docs.text:
The runtime registry is authoritative for selectable MATH components. Query it with:

harborrl options compat --json
harborrl options models --json
harborrl options algorithms --json
harborrl options tasks --json
harborrl options harnesses --json

Registry compatibility checks protocols, backend contracts, execution backends, Harbor versions, group size, and raw-logprob requirements. A passing combination is eligible for configuration; it is not live deployment evidence.

docs.title: Dataset metadata
docs.text:
harborrl options datasets --json reports each known dataset's status and whether its task files are locally bundled. Planned datasets are not ready to train, and an installed wheel does not contain repository examples.

HarborRL never downloads a dataset as a side effect of catalog browsing, validation, or configuration generation.

docs.title: Harbor Hub compatibility summary
docs.text:
The repository's public compatibility summary records scoped evidence about candidate Harbor task collections. Read its evidence level literally:

  • static evidence covers format or metadata inspection;
  • dynamic evidence covers the explicitly recorded execution scope; and
  • neither automatically proves end-to-end RL training, learning improvement, or support for every task in a collection.

docs.title: Acceptance levels
docs.text: Use the environment verification protocol to report one of cpu_development, deployment_preflight, or training. Do not promote a CPU test or dry run to a live-training claim.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
claude_code is the only registered harness. It speaks Anthropic Messages v1 to the HarborRL policy gateway and consumes Qwen tool calls through Harbor 0.23.0.

The bundled profile shape is:

{
  "agent_timeout_sec": 120,
  "cli_version": "2.1.141",
  "max_turns": 4,
  "model": "policy",
  "setup_timeout_sec": 300,
  "verifier_timeout_sec": 60
}

All six fields are required. disallowed_tools is the only optional field and must be a comma-separated identifier list. HarborRL always adds Agent and Task to the denylist.

docs.title: Runtime controls
docs.text:
For each attempt, the adapter:

  • requires an exact CLI version rather than latest;
  • injects a short-lived attempt credential and the plain gateway origin;
  • disables prompt caching, cache warmup, compaction, auto-memory, auto-update, and nonessential traffic;
  • sets max_thinking_tokens to zero and uses bypass-permissions mode inside the isolated task environment; and
  • strips ambient provider keys, Claude settings, and proxy credentials from the runner environment.

The repository example pins Claude Code 2.1.141. Other versions must be probed against the native session contract before use.

docs.title: Consumption audit
docs.text:
HTTP delivery is not considered proof that the harness consumed a model response. HarborRL parses the persisted native Claude session, requires one complete session, merges the known split-message form, rejects auxiliary/sidechain generations and summaries, and matches response IDs and content against gateway evidence.

The audit permits the locked CLI's special empty final end_turn form only when the terminal result provides matching success evidence.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Other harnesses are not registered.
  • Ambient credentials are intentionally rejected.
  • The configured gateway URL must be a plain HTTP(S) origin with no /v1 suffix, embedded credentials, query, or fragment.

docs.title: Qwen
docs.text:
qwen is the only registered model family. A configuration selects a Slime model preset through model.args_file; the value must begin with qwen and contain only letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens.

model:
  args_file: qwen3-8B
  checkpoint: /models/qwen3-8b
  reference: /models/qwen3-8b-reference

The example preset is a configuration name consumed by the pinned backend stack. A matching prefix alone does not prove that the checkpoint exists, fits in memory, or is compatible with a particular backend installation.

docs.title: Protocol path
docs.text:
Boundary Implemented contract Serving backend SGLang Harness request protocol Anthropic Messages v1 Generated tool protocol qwen-tool-call-v1 Training backend slime-v0.3.2-native-v1

The adapter renders messages with the tokenizer's chat template using enable_thinking=False, requires real nonnegative token IDs, and parses Qwen tool calls from generated text.

docs.title: Identity checks
docs.text:
The training schema requires two lowercase SHA-256 fingerprints:

  • gateway.tokenizer_digest identifies the tokenizer behavior used by rollout.
  • gateway.template_digest identifies the chat template.

The configuration wizard can calculate both using the selected GPU Python and local or SSH checkpoint. It loads tokenizer files offline with trust_remote_code=False; it does not download a model.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• No other model family is registered.
  • Memory fit is a live deployment concern, not a schema guarantee.
  • Tokenizer and template fingerprints are checked against runtime evidence.
  • Native consistency enforcement currently supports dense models with PP=CP=1; see train / inference consistency.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: HarborRL consumes native Harbor tasks and locks them into either a JSON list or a JSONL catalog. It does not maintain benchmark-specific conversion formats.

docs.title: Native task layout
docs.text:
task/
├── task.toml
├── instruction.md
├── environment/
│   └── Dockerfile
└── tests/
    └── test.sh

task.toml declares the environment, agent, resources, and verifier. instruction.md becomes the agent prompt. The verifier writes a reward artifact under /logs/verifier/ when Harbor executes the task.

docs.title: Registered providers
Inspect before locking
docs.text:
harborrl hub inspect \
  --tasks-dir /path/to/tasks \
  --dataset my-dataset \
  --revision pinned-revision \
  --run-dir ./task-inspection

Inspection is static and CPU-only. It writes immutable JSONL evidence plus a summary; it does not execute the task, allocate Docker, or establish trainability. Follow the task tutorial to turn valid inspection evidence into a catalog.

docs.title: Dataset claims
docs.text: Repository manifests distinguish bundled examples, planned sources, static checks, and dynamic evidence. A collection name or static compatibility result does not mean that HarborRL ships the tasks or has completed RL training on them. See compatibility.

docs.title: Run artifacts
docs.text:
HarborRL writes immutable or append-only evidence under a unique run directory. For native training the root is:

OUTPUT_ROOT/training/YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-XXXXXXXX/

Service mode uses deployment.storage.run_root; embedded mode uses training.output.root.

docs.title: Launch evidence
docs.text:
Artifact Purpose launch.json Resolved plan, run path, source evidence, materialized inputs effective-config.json Component IDs, environment mapping, versions, field usage effective-command.json Final executable argv after launcher expansion source-manifest.json Git commit, dirty flag, and source hashes source.patch Binary-capable diff of relevant tracked source changes source-new/ Copies of relevant untracked source files, when present config/native_catalog.json Normalized locked task entries config/native_tasks.jsonl Materialized prompt rows consumed by the backend

Source evidence covers HarborRL implementation, scripts, examples, and project metadata. Provider credentials and proxy values are deliberately excluded.

docs.title: Rollout evidence
docs.text:
native-rollouts/ contains group and attempt identities, gateway requests/responses, trace seals, Harbor results, verifier artifacts, reward receipts, Native IR v2, and group exports. Exact nesting follows run/group/slot identity rather than a human-editable filename convention.

Key invariants include:

  • task, harness, reward, sampling, tokenizer, and template identity;
  • one locked policy version per group;
  • confirmed response consumption;
  • immutable request/response and verifier digests;
  • no pending gateway requests at trace seal; and
  • complete groups before training export.
